quarterly_data.quarter: Western Digital Citi’s Global TMT Conference 2026 (09-09-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: SUPPLY, NOT DEMAND, IS THE GATE - AND CURRENT EXABYTE SUPPLY GROWTH IS ONLY LOW 20s: CFO Kris Sennesael was explicit that 'my revenue is not gated by the demand. My revenue is gated by the amount I can supply', and that Western Digital 'can't supply more than 25% right now, year-over-year growth in exabyte' while demand is running well above that. Fiscal 2026 exabyte growth was 'on or about 25% year-over-year', helped by one quarter at 34% against an easy compare, but the current run rate is 'low 20s, 22%, 23% year-over-year exabyte growth in supply' because the company is 'somewhat in between two product transitions' after four or five quarters of ramping 32TB ePMR. Three transitions are queued to re-accelerate supply: next-generation ePMR up to 40TB, first-generation HAMR up to 44TB, then a 50-plus TB generation, with a roadmap beyond to 70s and 100-plus TB per drive. He sees no digestion: every customer conversation comes back with a stronger demand signal and longer visibility.
quarterly_data.figure: supply more than 25% right now; low 20s, 22%, 23% year-over-year exabyte growth in supply; one quarter where we had 34%

quarterly_data.quarter: Western Digital Citi’s Global TMT Conference 2026 (09-09-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: LTA COVERAGE DISCLOSED BY YEAR FOR THE FIRST TIME - MOST OF 2027 LOCKED, SOME 2028, A SMALLER PART OF 2029: Sennesael said Western Digital builds to order, that 'it takes 52 weeks to produce a HDD' and that most customers are asked to place purchase orders at least 52 weeks in advance. On contract coverage: 'the vast majority of calendar or fiscal year 2027 is under LTA. Some of fiscal or calendar year 2028 is under LTA, and even a smaller part of fiscal or calendar year 2029 is under LTA', while customers want to secure supply in 2030 or 2031. The LTAs commit a base volume - 'typically less than what our customers want' - at a base price, with deliberate volume flexibility to the upside priced differently, which is part of why price per terabyte keeps improving. Pricing itself accelerated from 'up 9% year-over-year' two quarters ago to 'up 18%, 19% year-over-year' last quarter, and he sees 'still a little bit more room there to grow that' as higher-capacity drives deliver better rack density, real-estate and power TCO.
quarterly_data.figure: 52 weeks; vast majority of calendar or fiscal year 2027, is under LTA; Some of fiscal or calendar year 2028 is under LTA; even a smaller part of fiscal or calendar year 2029; up 9% year-over-year; up 18%, 19% year-over-year

quarterly_data.quarter: Western Digital Citi’s Global TMT Conference 2026 (09-09-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: HAMR IS IN QUALIFICATION AT FOUR LARGE HYPERSCALE CUSTOMERS: Sennesael said Western Digital is 'currently in qualification with four large hyperscale customers' for first-generation HAMR after almost 10 years of development, that qualifications are going really well with customers liking the areal density, reliability and quality, and that the intent is 'to start shipping in the first half of calendar year 2027, probably a little bit in Q1, a little bit more in Q2, and then continue to ramp that in Q3 and Q4 of calendar year 2027'. Not being first to HAMR helps because customers are already familiar with the technology, though they remain deliberately conservative in qualification. Meanwhile the 40TB ePMR, which shipped a little last quarter, 'will start ramping this quarter and then progressively more over the next couple of quarters'.
quarterly_data.figure: four large hyperscale customers; first half of calendar year 2027

quarterly_data.quarter: Western Digital Citi’s Global TMT Conference 2026 (09-09-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: HIGH-BANDWIDTH DRIVES WILL BE INTRODUCED IN THE +50TB RANGE AND ARE AIMED AT FLASH TERRITORY INCLUDING KV CACHE: Sennesael said the High-Bandwidth drives shown at Innovation Day were very well received and that Western Digital is 'shipping, I believe, five of our customers' engineering samples. Performance targets: 'we are now targeting a 2X improvement on the performance, but we have a 4 and an 8X that's in the works.' Introduction will be in the '+50 terabyte range' rather than on the 40TB or 44TB drives, because high performance matters more at higher capacities. The strategic point: roughly 80% of data sits on HDD with 15%-20% on SSD or flash purely because flash has an IO performance advantage, so 'as we continue to execute on those High-Bandwidth drives, we will be able to encroach into what is today the flash segment' - and KV caching for inference is one of those opportunities, addressable with higher-performance HDDs rather than a flash partnership.
quarterly_data.figure: 2X improvement on the performance; 4 and an 8X; +50 terabyte range

quarterly_data.quarter: Western Digital Citi’s Global TMT Conference 2026 (09-09-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: MEMORY INFLATION IS NOW AN INPUT COST INSIDE THE HDD, SLOWING THE COST-PER-TB CURVE: Sennesael reaffirmed the long-term target of cost per terabyte down 'on or about 10% year over year' but warned it will not hold every year - being between two product transitions temporarily slows it, and 'inside the HDD, we use a little bit of DRAM, and we use a little bit of NAND, and that has become a lot more expensive', with input cost increases across the supply chain creating near-term headwinds. He still expects gross margin to keep increasing at a pretty good pace given pricing, with gross margin now 'in the mid-50s' and operating margin 'in the mid-40s' and no ceiling he can identify. On investment: long-term CapEx is framed as 'in the range of 4%-6% to revenue', below that range the last couple of years and 'slightly above that range' the next couple of years, spent mainly on heads and media (including Western Digital's own substrate and media conversion) and on factory automation, which lifts unit output without major capacity CapEx. He sized the category for context: HDDs 'might only be 4% or 5% of the total CapEx spending of the big hyperscalers' but without them there is no AI.
quarterly_data.figure: on or about 10% year over year; in the range of 4%-6% to revenue; 4% or 5% of the total CapEx spending
